extracted.intended_audience: legislators, jurists, political philosophers, and students of comparative government
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for structuring judgments, procedural forms, and penalties across different government types (despotism, monarchy, republic), with comparative examples and practical safeguards. Intended to inform law- and policy-making about judicial procedure and punishment proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forming judgments differently by regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Dans les monarchies, les juges prennent la manière des arbitres: ils délibèrent ensemble, ils se communiquent leurs pensées, ils se concilient; ... A Rome, et dans les villes grecques, les juges ne se communiquaient point: chacun donnait son avis d'une de ces trois manières: j'absous, je condamne, il ne me paraît pas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that the mode of reaching judgment should fit the constitution: monarchies favor collective deliberation and adjustment of opinion; republics (or popular judgement) require clear, single issues so the people can vote. Example: Roman practice of three possible votes and the necessity in popular judgement to present one fact only. Implication: design judicial procedures to match political regime and audience; avoid practices (e.g., shifting factual framing) that confuse popular adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fixed procedural formulas to present a single question
rubrics_metrics.description: Les Romains, à l'exemple des Grecs, introduisirent des formules d'actions, et établirent la nécessité de diriger chaque affaire par l'action qui lui était propre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed action-formulas (formules d'actions) fix the state of the question so the people (or tribunal) always have one clear object before them. Without them, the state of the question would change continuously in a large affair, making judgement impossible. Practical guidance: procedural clarity and stable pleadings prevent confusion in adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit judge discretion vs allow 'actions de bonne foi'
rubrics_metrics.description: Les préteurs imaginèrent d'autres formules d'actions qu'on appela de bonne foi, où la manière de prononcer était plus dans la disposition du juge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tension between strict procedural claims (judge must grant only precise demand) and more discretionary 'ex bona fide' actions. Note that French jurists say 'En France toutes les actions sont de bonne foi.' Guidance: choose between formal predictability and judicial flexibility according to regime spirit (monarchy favors more discretion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign should not sit as judge in monarchies
rubrics_metrics.description: Dans les États despotiques, le prince peut juger lui-même. Il ne le peut dans les monarchies: la constitution serait détruite, les pouvoirs intermédiaires dépendants, anéantis; ... le prince serait le juge et la partie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that a sovereign judging would collapse constitutional balances, create conflicts of interest (sovereign as party and judge), eliminate formalities, spread fear, and destroy the legitimacy of clemency (grace). Gives historical examples (Louis XIII and the duke de la Valette) and Roman emperors (Claude, Néron) to illustrate abuses. Practical rule: separate sovereign/political functions from judicial decision-making in monarchies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural safeguards: exile before judgment and dedication of condemned goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Les législateurs de Rome firent deux choses: ils permirent aux accusés de s'exiler avant le jugement; et ils voulurent que les biens des condamnés fussent consacrés, pour que le peuple n'en eût pas la confiscation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures limited popular incentives to convict for gain and provided an exit that protected accused persons. Use procedural devices (voluntary exile, protection of property from confiscation) to reduce unjust popular convictions and align incentives of accusers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide review/appeal mechanisms to check popular passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Solon... voulut que l'aréopage revît l'affaire; que, s'il croyait l'accusé injustement absous, il l'accusât de nouveau devant le peuple: que, s'il le croyait injustement condamné, il arrêtât l'exécution, et lui fît rejuger l'affaire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a magistrature or higher body to review popular verdicts to correct both false acquittals and false convictions; also recommends procedural slowness when the accused is imprisoned so the people can calm and judge coldly. Practical guidance: appellate or supervisory review stabilizes justice in popular systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers (royal council) should not act as judges
rubrics_metrics.description: C'est encore un grand inconvénient dans la monarchie que les ministres du prince jugent eux-mêmes les affaires contentieuses... il y a, par la nature des choses, une espèce de contradiction entre le conseil du monarque et ses tribunaux.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes functions: royal councils (few persons, political, passionate) versus courts (many judges, dispassionate). Guidance: keep administrative/political advisement separate from judicial adjudication to preserve impartiality and the indifferent temperament required for justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid single magistrate rule except in despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: Un tel magistrat ne peut avoir lieu que dans le gouvernement despotique. On voit dans l'histoire romaine à quel point un juge unique peut abuser de son pouvoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single judges concentrate power and are prone to abuse (historical examples Appius, decemviri). Practical design: prefer collegial courts or multiple adjudicators except where the regime itself is despotic and centralized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control private informers; institute public prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Nous avons aujourd'hui une loi admirable: c'est celle qui veut que le prince, établi pour faire exécuter les lois, prépose un officier dans chaque tribunal pour poursuivre en son nom tous les crimes; de sorte que la fonction des délateurs est inconnue parmi nous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private delators under imperial regimes produced abuses and rewards for informers; assigning a public officer (prosecutor) to pursue crimes in the name of the state reduces opportunistic denunciations. If the public prosecutor abuses power, require him to name his denouncer—an accountability mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity of punishments should fit the type of government
rubrics_metrics.description: La sévérité des peines convient mieux au gouvernement despotique, dont le principe est la terreur, qu'à la monarchie et à la république, qui ont pour ressort l'honneur et la vertu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despotisms employ terror and harsh penalties; moderate states rely on honor, shame and prevention. A good legislator should focus more on preventing crimes by forming morals and using milder penalties, rather than inflicting harsh punishments. Comparative examples: Chinese authors' observation that increasing punishments precedes revolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties tend to vary with proximity to liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Il serait aisé de prouver que, dans tous ou presque tous les États d'Europe, les peines ont diminué ou augmenté à mesure qu'on s'est plus approché ou plus éloigné de la liberté.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical correlation: as states become freer, punishments moderate; as they become more despotic, punishments grow harsher. Use this as an interpretive rule when evaluating or reforming penal codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion punishments to the gravity of crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Il est essentiel que les peines aient de l'harmonie entre elles, parce qu'il est essentiel que l'on évite plutôt un grand crime qu'un moindre; ce qui attaque plus la société que ce qui la choque moins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates clear gradation of penalties (e.g., greater difference between theft and murder). Examples of pathological mismatches (same penalty for highway robbery and murder) lead to perverse incentives. Where formal differentiation is absent, use distinctions in hope of pardon (e.g., transport for thieves vs no pardon for murderers) to create practical differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use shame (infamy) as principal sanction where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Suivons la nature, qui a donné aux hommes la honte comme leur fléau; et que la plus grande partie de la peine soit l'infamie de la souffrir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Psychological/social sanctions (loss of honor, public shame) are effective in moderate societies and less corrosive than extreme corporal punishments. Lawmakers should harness reputation-based penalties alongside material sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive punishments undermine long-term efficacy and corrupt minds
rubrics_metrics.description: On use le ressort du gouvernement; l'imagination se fait à cette grande peine, comme elle s'était faite à la moindre... Lorsque le mal est une fois corrigé, on ne voit plus que la dureté du législateur; mais il reste un vice dans l'État, que cette dureté a produit: les esprits sont corrompus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harsh punishments initially restrain but eventually desensitize citizens and erode moral sentiments, producing corruption and habituation to cruelty. Example: wheel for highway robbery temporarily worked then crime returned; extreme military penalties produced despotism. Practical rule: avoid escalating to extreme punishments; attend to unintended long-term cultural effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pardon (letters of grace) as a moderating instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: C'est un grand ressort des gouvernements modérés que les lettres de grâces. ... Ce pouvoir que le prince a de pardonner, exécuté avec sagesse, peut avoir d'admirables effets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pardons allow differentiation and temper justice; they are unavailable in despotic regimes and their presence helps prevent severity's excess. Historical examples: Charles II remark, Henri IV's clemency, missed opportunities by Charles I and Louis XIII. Design guidance: retain discretionary clemency to modulate penalties and promote reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torture/questioning of criminals is not a necessary practice
rubrics_metrics.description: La question contre les criminels n'est pas dans un cas forcé... Nous voyons aujourd'hui une nation très bien policée la rejeter sans inconvénients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many authorities oppose torture; some nations (England) reject it and manage policing without it. Ancient rules limited torture (Athenians, Romans with restrictions). Practical guidance: eliminate or strictly limit torture; use other evidentiary standards and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance pecuniary and corporal punishments according to social context
rubrics_metrics.description: Nos pères les Germains n'admettaient guère que des peines pécuniaires... Les Japonais, au contraire, rejettent ces sortes de peines, sous prétexte que les gens riches éluderaient la punition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither fines nor corporal punishments are universally ideal: fines can be proportioned to fortune and combined with infamy; corporal punishments may be appropriate in some societies. A good legislator seeks a middle course, adapting penalties to social character and ensuring proportionality and non-evasion by the wealthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of talion should be tempered or convertible to compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Les États despotiques... usent beaucoup de la loi du talion; les États modérés la reçoivent quelquefois: mais ... les autres lui donnent presque toujours des tempéraments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talion (eye for an eye) works as strict retribution in despotic regimes, but moderate states temper it, allow reconciliation or conversion to monetary damages (as in Roman law of the Twelve Tables). Design rule: temper strict reciprocity with compensatory options to reduce cruelty and practical harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid collective punishment of families for individual crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: On punit à la Chine les pères pour les fautes de leurs enfants. ... Ceci est encore tiré des idées despotiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishing parents for children's crimes derives from despotic ideas about collective responsibility and dishonor. In societies valuing honor, social shame suffices; legal design should avoid penalizing innocent relatives and instead rely on targeted sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate penalties by social rank and public dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: On divisa les peines en trois classes: celles qui regardaient les premières personnes de l'État... celles qu'on infligeait aux personnes d'un rang inférieur... enfin celles qui ne concernaient que les conditions basses, et qui furent les plus rigoureuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically penalties were stratified by rank (sublimiores, medii, infimi). While criticized implicitly, the text records that emperors tended to soften penalties for high ranks and harden them for lower ranks. Guidance: be aware of social stratification in punishment design and its political effects; reformers should consider the justice and stability implications of rank-based sentencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent judicial corruption by insulating courts from sovereign/palace influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Les lois sont les yeux du prince, il voit par elles ce qu'il ne pourrait pas voir sans elles. Veut-il faire la fonction des tribunaux, il travaille non pas pour lui, mais pour ses séducteurs contre lui.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sovereign assumes judicial functions, judgment becomes subject to courtly influence and sale of justice (historical examples under Justinian and later emperors). Practical measure: maintain institutional separation, open courts, and legal mechanisms to prevent sale of judgments and palace interference.
